context: Attribute names with labels, levels, role, clinical description, physical/epidemiological mechanism, and directional dependency hints (known upstream drivers and downstream effects) — structured to support causal discovery without fully specifying the DAG.

variables.name: dysp
variables.label: Dyspnoea
variables.description: Shortness of breath reported by the patient.
variables.mechanism: Dyspnoea arises when ventilatory demand exceeds capacity; in this model it is caused by bronchitis (airway obstruction and mucus hypersecretion) and by the tuberculosis-or-cancer state (via parenchymal destruction, pleural involvement, or mass effect). It does not itself cause any other modeled variable.

variables.name: tub
variables.label: Tuberculosis
variables.description: Pulmonary tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
variables.mechanism: TB risk is elevated by travel to high-prevalence regions (visit to Asia). TB produces parenchymal infiltrates visible on X-ray and contributes to dyspnoea through the shared 'either' node. It is causally independent of smoking and bronchitis in this model.

variables.name: lung
variables.label: Lung cancer
variables.mechanism: Lung cancer probability is raised by smoking via carcinogen-induced DNA damage. It contributes to both an abnormal chest X-ray and, through the 'either' node, to dyspnoea. It is causally independent of Asia travel and bronchitis given smoking.

variables.name: bronc
variables.label: Bronchitis
variables.mechanism: Bronchitis is strongly driven by smoking (ciliary paralysis, mucus hypersecretion, chronic irritation). It directly causes dyspnoea through airway obstruction. It does not influence the chest X-ray or the 'either' node in this model.

variables.name: asia
variables.label: Visit to Asia
variables.description: Recent travel to a region with high tuberculosis prevalence.
variables.mechanism: A root node (no modeled parents). Geographic exposure elevates TB prior probability due to higher regional incidence rates. It has no direct effect on cancer, bronchitis, smoking, or any diagnostic variable; its influence propagates exclusively through the tuberculosis node.

variables.name: smoke
variables.label: Smoking
variables.description: Current or recent tobacco smoking status.
variables.mechanism: A root node (no modeled parents). Smoking is the primary shared cause of both lung cancer and bronchitis in this network, making it the key common-cause confounder between those two diseases. Its influence does not extend directly to tuberculosis, X-ray, or dyspnoea except through its disease children.

variables.name: xray
variables.label: Chest X-ray abnormal
variables.mechanism: The X-ray is an effect node whose probability of being positive is elevated by the 'either' node (i.e., by TB or lung cancer). It has low specificity: both TB infiltrates and malignant masses produce similar radiographic appearances, so a positive X-ray cannot distinguish between them. X-ray does not cause any other modeled variable.

variables.name: either
variables.label: Tuberculosis or lung cancer present
variables.description: Deterministic OR of tuberculosis and lung cancer; yes if either or both are present.
variables.mechanism: Intermediate aggregation node that routes the combined causal influence of tuberculosis and lung cancer to their shared downstream effects (chest X-ray and dyspnoea). This node is the reason X-ray cannot discriminate between the two diseases: both feed into it identically. It has no parents outside of TB and lung cancer.
